findings.evidence:
template/scripts/github_read_cache.py:330-334: `stdout.partition("

")` runs first and `replace("
", "
")` only runs as a fallback. A CRLF response that has a literal `

` in its body would be cut there, which drops part of the body or puts body text in the headers. Every test transcript in tests/test_github_read_cache.py and the acceptance fake in parallel_lifecycle_acceptance.py uses LF only, so the CRLF path is never exercised. The design's own Risks section says the gh transcript parsing is covered by recorded transcripts, but none are recorded.
findings.summary: `parse_response` splits on a bare `\n\n` before it normalises CRLF. Real `gh api -i` output uses CRLF line endings, so the first partition can miss the header/body boundary or split at a blank line inside the body.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/github_read_cache.py:288-327: `_load` parses and structure-checks all entries on every `_page` call. `_store` rewrites the whole file on every 200. Entries are keyed per URL and nothing removes closed PRs or old Requirements. The overview reads many PRs in parallel, so with a large cache every 200 re-serialises the full file under the flock. The cost scales with accumulated history, not with the current candidate set.
findings.summary: Cache entries are never evicted, and every read and write loads and validates the whole file. Cost grows with the history of PRs and comment pages seen.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/managed_task.py:268-278: `_issue_read_env[str(root)]` is set once and never invalidated. Later calls skip `github_cli_env`, so a changed or expired gh login is not re-detected in that process. Tests that patch `github_cli_env` per case can see state left by earlier tests. The proposal does not mention this change.
findings.summary: `managed_task.fetch_issue` now keeps the result of a successful `github_cli_env` check in a process-global dict. This is a behaviour change outside the stated scope, and it can leak between tests or long-lived processes.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/lifecycle_workers.py:1211-1217 passes `Path.cwd()` to `read_cache.cached_gh_json`. `cache_path` (github_read_cache.py:273-277) calls `run_git(... --git-common-dir)`. A failure there is not a `GithubReadError`, so the `WorkerError` mapping does not apply. `main` catches only `(WorkerError, ValueError, GithubReadCacheError)`, so such a failure may surface as a traceback rather than a clean exit 2. No test covers a worker started outside a repository.
findings.summary: The worker `_gh_json` now needs a git checkout at `Path.cwd()` even for plain `gh api` reads. A non-git cwd fails in `run_git` inside `cache_path`, where before it ran `gh` directly.
